_why_no_T: JSON has no comment syntax and `Recipe` does not deny unknown fields, so this
array is how this file records a decision a reader would otherwise have to guess
at. It is data nothing reads.
The disc's `OS-Version3.9/Workbench3.5` holds 16 top-level drawers; the rules
below place 14. `T` and `WBStartup` are the two left out, and both are
deliberate rather than overlooked:
`T` is AmigaDOS's temporary directory, and on a running 3.9 system it is not
on SYS: at all. Measured on the owner's own AmigaOS39.iso (2026-08-19): the
disc's own `S/Startup-Sequence` — the file this recipe *does* place — runs
`C:MakeDir RAM:T RAM:Clipboards RAM:ENV RAM:ENV/Sys` and then
`Assign >NIL: T: RAM:T`, so `T:` is made in RAM at every boot and the disc's
copy is never consulted. The disc's `T` drawer is also empty (0 entries, by
7-Zip). AmigaOS 3.2's tree, which ART built and which booted to a clean
Workbench under WinUAE, likewise carries no `T` and its own Startup-Sequence
does the identical two lines. Copying an empty drawer whose assign points
elsewhere would place a directory the system never looks at.
`WBStartup` belongs to the second, unwritten half of this recipe rather than
to `workbench-base`: it is where a system's own startup programs are chosen,
and which ones a 3.9 tree should carry is one of the things the boot test
(spec section 4) was meant to establish and did not, because no 3.9 tree has
been booted yet.
If a boot disagrees with either judgement, add the rule then, with the run as
the reason — that is what a real run is for.
